eyebrow: CHARITY RESEARCH · BAY AREA · VIOLENCE PREVENTION
program: Whole-gift violence prevention, intervention and healing

nutshell.headline: A credible local violence-intervention mechanism, but no verified marginal gift price or capacity gap.
nutshell.body: Our signed prior-weighted illustration is $27.34M donor / $28.08M gross resources per 10 modeled QALYs. All quantified benefit is in Oakland/Alameda. The favorable 5% scenario supplies 66.1% of expected benefit; this is not a verified marginal donation offer.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Locally pioneered hospital-based peer intervention addresses violent reinjury, with encouraging but low-quality pooled evidence.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The organization's uncontrolled non-reinjury rate is not a causal effect. A current $5M state award makes new-gift additionality uncertain, and the QALY anchor is a model with important limitations.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain the current CalVIP budget, unique referral/enrollment/completion and waitlist flow, comparison-group outcomes, partner resources and a priced next-gift staffing plan.

programSection.body: Youth ALIVE! (EIN 94-3143254) serves Oakland through Caught in the Crossfire hospital intervention, violence interruption, Pathways mentoring, Teens on Target, counseling, homicide-family support and advocacy.

steps.title: Reach survivors at the bedside
steps.detail: Caught in the Crossfire specialists offer safety, healing and practical support after violent injury, aiming to prevent retaliation and recurrence.

steps.title: Support youth, families and neighborhoods
steps.detail: 2025 reported 118 CiC clients, 260 mediations, 131 bedside assessments, 72 Pathways youth, 70 families, 91 counseling clients/3,255 hours; overlap unknown. These counts are not summed as distinct beneficiaries.

steps.title: Change practice and policy
steps.detail: Youth ALIVE supports community prevention and advocacy; replication and policy spillovers receive no modeled QALYs.

programSection.boundary: All gift cash is charged. Only CiC-like service receives QALYs; violence interruption, Pathways, TNT, counseling, family support, and policy are zero-credit. FY2024 whole-organization expense was $7,305,670. Program allocation is a judgment, not an observed expense share; this is a partial-health model of a whole gift.

model.headline: $27.34M per 10 modeled Bay Area QALYs; giving HOLD.
model.body: Only an additional CiC-like course receives quantified health. The directly reported five-year modeled difference is 4.64−4.62=.020 QALY per participant, reduced by evidence-transfer and gift-additionality priors. No lifetime extrapolation is added.

inputs.label: CiC allocation
inputs.basis: The ordinary gift spans the full organization. Other activities retain costs but receive no separate health credit.

inputs.label: Funding additionality and realization
inputs.basis: Public contracts and the new state award may fund activity without the gift. Enrollment and completion also constrain delivery.

inputs.label: Cost per added client
inputs.basis: The favorable floor is $267,294 divided by 180 minimum comprehensive clients in the July2023–September2024 county contract. It is not a current marginal offer or complete resource cost.

inputs.label: Five-year QALY anchor
inputs.confidence: Limited modeled evidence; transfer is judgmental
inputs.basis: NICE summarizes a five-year undiscounted healthcare-payer Markov model, not observed trial QALYs. Potentially serious limitations and no probabilistic sensitivity analysis. Negative transfer represents a harm stress.

inputs.label: External resources per realized client
inputs.basis: Induced partner/clinical/housing/education resources are added to all donor cash; incomplete, not a lower bound. Index-injury emergency costs excluded; avoided costs not netted.

inputs.label: Bay / SF share
inputs.basis: Quantified CiC-like delivery is Oakland/Alameda. No direct SF delivery or additional policy/replication spillover is credited.

sensitivity.headline: −0.0048 QALY
sensitivity.detail: Signed burden stress, not an observed Youth ALIVE harm.

sensitivity.headline: Not defined
sensitivity.detail: No positive QALY; cost ratios null.

sensitivity.headline: $27.34M donor / $28.08M gross
sensitivity.detail: 0.036582 QALY; removing the favorable case gives $76.61M donor per10.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Weights and transfer inputs are analyst priors, not confidence intervals. Zero funding produces zero QALYs and null cost/geography/tail ratios. Published cost records conflict: PubMed reports $3,574/$3,515 and a $2,941 ICER; NICE reports $3,574/$3,015 and $27,950. We use the directly reported QALY difference rather than reverse-engineering a preferred cost pair.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2024 revenue $8.894M, expense $7.306M, surplus $1.588M and net assets $5.186M; $5.379M program-service revenue. A $5M CalVIP Cohort5 award covers April2026–September2029, with service through March2029. This is funding, not modeled health. No current waitlist, restricted-award budget or priced next-client plan is verified. Health-producing marginal room remains unpriced.

evidence.design: local five-year undiscounted healthcare-payer Markov model
evidence.population: Chong et al. 2015 + NICE Appendix H
evidence.transfer: not observed donor impact; NICE found potentially serious limitations; published $3,015/$3,515 comparator-cost and ICER records conflict
no concurrent counterfactual; complement is not effectiveness

reservations: The five-year QALY anchor is modeled, not trial-measured; the source has potentially serious limitations.
2026 pooled evidence is low quality and heterogeneous.
Current contract funding may displace new donations.
Ordinary-gift allocation, marginal client price and external resources are uncertain.
Other portfolio benefits remain unquantified, not proven absent.
excludedBenefits: Counseling and family support outside the credited CiC course
